subject.title: fix(codex): clean final/yield turn close writes a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout

question: Should Codex turns with an explicit terminal delivery await native `turn/completed` for up to 10 seconds, with immediate fallback interruption on new inbound input, instead of preserving the current immediate-stop behavior?
rationale: The implementation is technically bounded and proof-backed, but the grace-window duration, post-final lifecycle ownership, and new-inbound interruption policy are user-visible terminal semantics rather than a purely mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
options.body: Accept the 10-second absolute deadline and immediate new-inbound fallback after a rebase and upstream Codex contract review.

options.title: Keep immediate interruption
options.body: Preserve current terminal-stop timing and accept the Codex rollout marker as the existing protocol tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt the direction with revised policy
options.body: Keep the natural-completion seam but choose a different deadline or inbound-handling rule before implementation is refreshed.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
recommendation.body: Accept the 10-second absolute deadline and immediate new-inbound fallback after a rebase and upstream Codex contract review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current Codex source-reply finalization behavior that this PR changes after explicit terminal delivery.
